title: Edie's Sparkly Secret
markdown:
Headmistress Plum announced a picnic at Puddle Pond. Sandwiches, crisps, cheese, and blankets. Edie the duck waddled near, excited. Cas the cat stretched beside her.

The lemonade wasn’t sparkly.

Sunbeams striped the grass as Plum laid out the feast. Cheese cubes sat like tiny soldiers. Sandwiches piled high. But Edie saw the lemonade. Pale. Quiet. Her grandmother always added sugar crystals that made it fizz like captured stars.

The lemonade wasn’t sparkly.

A wobbly feeling twisted in Edie’s tummy. She wanted to speak, but her beak felt heavy. Cas nudged her. “Quack?” he purred. Edie looked at the pale jug and felt a tiny tear. A cloud darkened her picnic day.

Plum noticed drooping wings. “Is something amiss, dear Edie?” Edie wanted to say the lemonade wasn’t sparkly, but the words were stuck.

Cas chased a butterfly, tumbling in a flurry of fur. A moment to think. Edie took a shaky breath, picturing her grandmother’s smile.

“Headmistress Plum,” she whispered, a tiny puff, but steady. “My grandmother’s lemonade always has… little sparkly bits. For the fizz. For the sparkle.”

Plum’s eyes twinkled. She reached into her special basket. “Ah, Edie. I brought your grandmother’s secret sunshine sparks.” She sprinkled them in. Instantly the pitcher fizzed and popped, tiny golden lights dancing.

The lemonade was sparkly.

Edie watched, heart swelling. She had spoken up. The lemonade, magnificent with bubbly light, tasted like sunshine and happy laughter. She gulped. Fizzy sweetness tickled her beak. Cas purred on a blanket. Plum smiled. Warmth spread through Edie. A brave little voice had made the picnic fizz.

And the lemonade was sparkly at last.
characters: Edie (a duck), Cas (a cat), Plum (a headmistress)
